title: The first anti-AI protester to be jailed has a message for OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta: ‘Regain your humanity’
excerpt: Wynd Kaufmyn, 69, chained and locked the front doors of OpenAI’s headquarters last year with members of StopAI
content_html:
An activist who blocked the entrance to one of the world’s biggest AI companies is believed to have become the first person jailed for protesting against artificial intelligence as supporters dub her the “Rosa Parks of AI risk”.

Wynd Kaufmyn, 69, surrendered herself on Friday to authorities in San Francisco. She was found guilty by a jury for her role in an action last year that saw members of the group StopAI chain and lock the front doors of OpenAI’s headquarters in protest against the pursuit of artificial superintelligence.

The retired teacher from Berkeley, California, refused to move from a sit-in protest in February 2025 and pleaded not guilty to multiple misdemeanor charges. She was convicted in June of interfering with a business, trespassing with intent to interfere with a business, unlawful assembly and refusal to disperse at a riot. On Friday, sheriff’s officers handcuffed her as fellow campaigners sang to the tune of the Battle Hymn of the Republic (Glory, Glory Hallelujah): “Rise up, rise up and join us/Do not let the tech bros destroy us.”

“It’s absolutely frightening and appalling that these CEOs and AI experts know the dangers and they are pursuing it anyway,” Kaufmyn said before she was imprisoned. “That to me is unconscionable and reprehensible.”

She said she was willing to go to jail not because she was a martyr but because it was an “issue of sounding the alarm, challenging the system and hopefully trying to get the message out”.

Brooke Jenkins, the San Francisco district attorney, said the guilty verdict sent “a resounding message rejecting the notion that protesters can endanger public safety as a means to an end”.

As Kaufmyn was led out from the court, her supporters called out: “Stop AI” and: “Free Wynd” as the sheriff’s officer yelled: “Clear the court” and the judge admonished the protesters.

Dwight Ost, 73, one of two dozen other StopAI activists at the courthouse, called Kaufmyn “a brave and courageous woman”.

“There’s an existential threat that I believe in,” he said. “They can’t control it, and even the so-called experts don’t know what it’s about.”

Kaufmyn had argued that the protest was a necessity and that she believed she was allowed to act to prevent a greater harm from happening. Since the lobby sit-in last year, some of the biggest AI labs, including OpenAI and Anthropic, have reported their models escaping the confinements of experiments.

This week, the US senator Bernie Sanders demanded tech leaders pause AI development, citing fears that, in the wrong hands, it might “lead to new bioweapons that result in the deaths of tens of millions of people”.

Meanwhile, more than a thousand researchers at frontier AI labs this summer signed a letter warning of “a real risk that capability development rapidly accelerates beyond our ability to understand or control the resulting systems”.

Frontier AI labs are locked in a race to create more capable AI models as the companies target IPOs that are forecast to reach valuations in the trillions of dollars. At the same time, Washington is competing with Beijing for supremacy in the fast-developing technology, creating a disincentive for tougher safety regulation.

“The jury rejected [Kaufmyn’s] necessity defence, but as the first person to go to jail over this, Wynd Kaufmyn could go down in history as the Rosa Parks of AI risk,” said David Kreuger, a University of Montreal AI safety expert who has warned AI “may literally lead to human extinction, in the same way that humans have caused many other species to go extinct”. Parks was a Black woman who refused to give up her bus seat for a white passenger in contravention of racist segregation laws in 1950s Alabama, a catalyzing incident for the US civil rights movement of the ensuing decade.

Kaufmyn spoke on the eve of her imprisonment from her shingled house in Berkeley, which is festooned with Mexican tiles and pro-Gaza signs. She played down the Parks parallel, pointing out her short sentence – one week, but said the comparison had also crossed the campaign group’s mind, given that she is thought to be the first AI protester jailed.

She said that when she was found guilty, she was “hit with a wave of grief” because she realised her peers “just didn’t get” the danger she believes is posed by the race to superintelligence. But she was beginning to feel “vindicated” as more prominent figures like Sanders were speaking out. She is now braced for the prison experience of an orange jump suit, “horrible food, dirt [and] you can’t sleep”. She has been previously jailed for short periods related to her decades of political activism over causes including Nicaragua, nuclear disarmament, western Sahara and Palestine.

Her message to the chief executives of OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, which also reported a security incident with its model, was “regain your humanity”. Kaufmyn said her target audience was ordinary people “and the message being: stop the progress of this technology. Let’s get a global ban on the race to superintelligence.”

Professor Stuart Russell, a leading AI professor at the University of California at Berkeley and president of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI, gave evidence in Kaufmyn’s defence. He claimed OpenAI’s activities “pose an unacceptable risk”, alleging it had deployed AI systems with inadequate safeguards. He said that further development of these systems “must be conditioned on rigorous guarantees of safety, which are currently unavailable”.

Russell said: “Wynd stood up for her beliefs and is being punished.” He said her beliefs seemed reasonable but “what is unreasonable is allowing a process to continue whereby private entities knowingly create a substantial extinction risk for private gain”.

StopAI has been roiled by its own controversies. Last November, its co-founder, Sam Kirchner, 27, went missing after an internal bust-up over whether or not to use violent tactics. He is said to have told colleagues the “non-violence ship has sailed”, raising concerns he might take violent action against OpenAI employees. StopAI aims to pursue non-violent direct action.

OpenAI was approached for comment.

He said that further development of these systems “must be conditioned on rigorous guarantees of safety, which are currently unavailable”.

blocks.html_en: Russell said: “Wynd stood up for her beliefs and is being punished.” He said her beliefs seemed reasonable but “what is unreasonable is allowing a process to continue whereby private entities knowingly create a substantial extinction risk for private gain”.

blocks.html_en: StopAI has been roiled by its own controversies. Last November, its co-founder, Sam Kirchner, 27, went missing after an internal bust-up over whether or not to use violent tactics. He is said to have told colleagues the “non-violence ship has sailed”, raising concerns he might take violent action against OpenAI employees. StopAI aims to pursue non-violent direct action.

content_html_zh:
一名封锁全球最大人工智能公司入口的活动人士据信成为第一个因抗议人工智能而入狱的人，支持者称她为“人工智能风险的罗莎·帕克斯”。

69 岁的 Wynd Kaufmyn 于周五向旧金山当局自首。 去年，StopAI 组织的成员锁上了 OpenAI 总部的前门，以抗议对人工智能的追求，陪审团裁定她有罪。

这位来自加利福尼亚州伯克利的退休教师拒绝离开 2025 年 2 月的静坐抗议活动，并对多项轻罪指控表示不认罪。 她于六月被判犯有干扰商业、意图干扰商业、非法集会和在骚乱中拒绝解散等罪名。 周五，治安官给她戴上手铐，其他活动人士唱着共和国战歌（荣耀，荣耀哈利路亚）：“站起来，站起来，加入我们/不要让科技兄弟摧毁我们。”

考夫明在入狱前表示：“这些首席执行官和人工智能专家知道其中的危险，但他们仍然在追求它，这绝对是令人恐惧和震惊的。” “这对我来说是不合理且应受谴责的。”

她说，她愿意入狱，不是因为她是烈士，而是因为这是一个“拉响警报、挑战体制并希望试图传达信息的问题”。

旧金山地区检察官布鲁克·詹金斯表示，有罪判决发出了“一个响亮的信息，驳斥了抗议者可以危及公共安全作为达到目的的手段的观点”。

当考夫明被带出法庭时，她的支持者高喊：“停止人工智能”和“释放温德”，而治安官则高喊：“清场”，法官对抗议者进行训诫。

73 岁的德怀特·奥斯特 (Dwight Ost) 是法院内另外两打 StopAI 活动人士之一，他称考夫明是“一位勇敢的女性”。

“我相信存在一种生存威胁，”他说。 “他们无法控制，就连所谓的专家也不知道这是怎么回事。”

考夫明辩称，抗议是必要的，她相信自己可以采取行动，以防止发生更大的伤害。 自去年的大厅静坐以来，一些最大的人工智能实验室，包括 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，都报告说他们的模型摆脱了实验的限制。

本周，美国参议员伯尼·桑德斯 (Bernie Sanders) 要求科技领袖暂停人工智能开发，理由是担心人工智能如果落入坏人之手，可能会“催生新的生物武器，导致数千万人死亡”。

与此同时，今年夏天，前沿人工智能实验室的一千多名研究人员签署了一封信，警告“能力发展迅速加速超出我们理解或控制最终系统的能力的真正风险”。

前沿人工智能实验室正在竞相创建更强大的人工智能模型，因为这些公司的目标是首次公开募股，预计估值将达到数万亿美元。 与此同时，华盛顿正在与北京争夺快速发展的技术的霸主地位，这阻碍了更严格的安全监管。

蒙特利尔大学人工智能安全专家戴维·克鲁格 (David Kreuger) 表示：“陪审团驳回了 [Kaufmyn] 的必要性抗辩，但作为第一个因此入狱的人，Wynd Kaufmyn 可能会作为人工智能风险领域的罗莎·帕克斯 (Rosa Parks) 载入史册。”他警告说，人工智能“实际上可能会导致人类灭绝，就像人类导致许多其他物种灭绝一样”。 帕克斯是一名黑人妇女，她拒绝在公交车上为白人乘客让座，这违反了 20 世纪 50 年代阿拉巴马州的种族主义隔离法，这一事件催化了随后十年的美国民权运动。

考夫明在入狱前夕在伯克利的木瓦房子里发表了讲话，房子里挂满了墨西哥瓷砖和支持加沙的标志。 她淡化了帕克斯的相似之处，指出她的刑期很短——一周，但她表示，考虑到她被认为是第一个被监禁的人工智能抗议者，竞选团队也考虑过这种比较。

她说，当她被判有罪时，她“感到一阵悲痛”，因为她意识到她的同龄人“只是没有意识到”她认为超级智能竞赛带来的危险。 但随着桑德斯等更多知名人物的发声，她开始感到“被证明是正确的”。 现在，她已经准备好迎接穿着橙色连体服的监狱经历，“可怕的食物、污垢，[而且]你无法入睡”。 她此前曾因数十年来在尼加拉瓜、核裁军、西撒哈拉和巴勒斯坦等问题上的政治活动而被短期监禁。

她向 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 的首席执行官传达的信息是“恢复你的人性”，该公司也报告了其模型的安全事件。 考夫明说，她的目标受众是普通人，“传达的信息是：停止这项技术的进步。 让我们在全球范围内禁止超级智能竞赛。”

加州大学伯克利分校人工智能首席教授、国际安全与道德人工智能协会主席 Stuart Russell 教授为 Kaufmyn 的辩护提供了证据。 他声称 OpenAI 的活动“构成了不可接受的风险”，并声称其部署的人工智能系统缺乏足够的保障措施。 他表示，这些系统的进一步开发“必须以严格的安全保障为条件，而目前尚无法做到这一点”。

拉塞尔说：“温德坚持自己的信仰，正在受到惩罚。” 他说，她的信念似乎是合理的，但“不合理的是允许私人实体故意为私人利益制造巨大的灭绝风险”。

StopAI 因其自身的争议而饱受争议。 去年 11 月，其联合创始人、27 岁的萨姆·基什内尔 (Sam Kirchner) 在一场关于是否使用暴力策略的内部争吵后失踪。 据说他告诉同事“非暴力之船已经起航”，引发了人们对他可能对 OpenAI 员工采取暴力行动的担忧。 StopAI 旨在追求非暴力直接行动。

记者联系 OpenAI 征求意见。
